title: CyberPowerPC Unveils RTX Founders Edition Pre‑Built PCs Starting at $1,549 – TechPowerUp Review
body:
CyberPowerPC has announced a limited‑edition line of pre‑built gaming rigs that ship with NVIDIA’s coveted RTX 50‑series “Founders Edition” graphics cards, starting at $1,549. The move coincides with the annual GeForce Week celebration and marks one of the few occasions where the premium Founders Edition GPUs, typically sold only through NVIDIA’s own storefront, appear in a third‑party system. The new configurations—featuring the RTX 5090, RTX 5080, and RTX 5070 Founders Editions—target enthusiasts who want top‑tier performance without the hassle of building a PC from scratch.

The partnership between CyberPowerPC and NVIDIA is notable because it sidesteps the usual distribution model for Founders Edition cards. Historically, NVIDIA has limited these reference designs to its own website and select retail partners, positioning them as a showcase of the company’s engineering prowess rather than a mass‑market product. By bundling the cards with ready‑made systems, CyberPowerPC not only expands the reach of the RTX 50‑series but also taps into a growing segment of gamers who prefer turnkey solutions. The company has emphasized that the launch will be a “limited run,” suggesting that inventory will be scarce and likely to sell out quickly during the promotional window.

The base model, priced at $1,549, pairs an RTX 5070 Founders Edition with a 12th‑generation Intel Core i7 processor, 16 GB of DDR5 RAM, a 1 TB NVMe SSD, and a 750 W power supply. Higher‑tier options climb to $2,299 for the RTX 5080 and $2,899 for the RTX 5090, each adding more CPU power, additional memory, and larger storage capacities. All configurations retain CyberPowerPC’s signature RGB lighting and customizable chassis, allowing buyers to personalize the aesthetic while enjoying the reference cooling solution that NVIDIA designed for the cards. The company also offers a “Build‑Your‑Own” portal where customers can swap components, though the Founders Edition GPU remains the fixed centerpiece.

Industry analysts see this launch as a strategic test for NVIDIA’s distribution flexibility. By allowing a reputable system integrator to sell the Founders Edition, NVIDIA can gauge demand outside its own ecosystem and potentially unlock new revenue streams. Moreover, the timing aligns with the broader rollout of the RTX 50‑series, which promises up to 2× the ray‑tracing performance of the previous generation thanks to the new Ada Lovelace architecture and advanced AI‑driven features such as DLSS 3.5. For gamers, the availability of these cards in pre‑built form reduces the barrier to entry for next‑gen titles that heavily leverage real‑time ray tracing and high frame‑rate demands.

Consumer reaction has been mixed. On one hand, many enthusiasts welcome the convenience of a ready‑made system that includes the most powerful GPU on the market. On the other, purists argue that the Founders Edition’s reference design is often outperformed by custom AIB (add‑in‑board) variants that feature higher boost clocks, larger cooling solutions, and factory overclocks. CyberPowerPC counters this by highlighting the Founders Edition’s superior power efficiency and the fact that its reference cooler is engineered to run quietly under load—attributes that appeal to gamers who value a balance between performance and noise levels.

The launch also underscores the competitive pressure on other PC manufacturers such as Dell’s Alienware, HP’s Omen, and MSI, all of which have announced plans to incorporate RTX 50‑series GPUs in upcoming models. As the RTX 50‑series matures, price points are expected to gradually drop, potentially making high‑end gaming more accessible. However, supply chain constraints and the ongoing global chip shortage could keep inventory tight, especially for the top‑tier RTX 5090 Founders Edition rigs.

Looking ahead, CyberPowerPC’s limited‑edition offering may set a precedent for future collaborations between GPU makers and system integrators. If the response proves strong, we could see more frequent inclusion of flagship GPUs in pre‑built packages, blurring the line between boutique custom builds and mass‑market desktops. For now, gamers eager to experience the full capabilities of NVIDIA’s latest architecture have a new, albeit fleeting, avenue to do so without the complexities of a DIY build.
